questions.stem: A 2.0 kg ball is dropped from rest from a height of 5.0 m; find its speed just before impact (m/s).

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: What makes a force conservative
questions.learningObjective: Identify which forces are conservative
questions.stem: Which of the following forces is conservative in the usual sense?

options.text: Friction between a block and a rough surface
Tension in a rope pulling a cart at constant speed
options.misconception: assumes any constant force does no work

options.text: Air resistance on a falling parachute

questions.explanation: Gravity is conservative because work done is path independent and energy is stored as potential energy. Friction and drag are non-conservative and dissipate energy.

questions.stem: A planet has radius 6.4e6 m and surface gravity 9.8 m/s^2; compute escape speed (m/s).
questions.explanation: Escape speed equals sqrt(2gR). Substituting g 9.8 and R 6.4e6 gives about 1.12e4 m/s. This matches Earth-like values.

questions.explanation: Momentum conservation gives (3*4+1*0)/(3+1)=3 m/s. Kinetic energy is not conserved in this perfectly inelastic collision.

Kinetic energy after collision to kinetic energy before

questions.topic: Confusing an angular rate with a linear speed
questions.learningObjective: Convert angular speed to revolutions per minute
questions.stem: A motor shaft rotates at 10 rad/s; find speed in rev/min (approx).
questions.explanation: rev/min = omega*60/(2 pi) = 10*60/6.283 = 95.5. Radians are dimensionless in this conversion.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: A pendulum released from the horizontal
questions.learningObjective: Compute period of simple pendulum
questions.stem: A simple pendulum has length 1.0 m; find its period (s) using g=9.8.
questions.explanation: T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) = 2 pi sqrt(1/9.8) = 2.01 s. Period is independent of mass and amplitude for small angles.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: What is conserved when two bodies stick together
questions.learningObjective: Compute energy loss fraction in inelastic collision
questions.stem: In a perfectly inelastic collision of equal masses with one initially at rest, the fraction of kinetic energy lost is?
questions.explanation: Initial KE = half m v^2. Final speed v/2, final KE = half*(2m)*(v/2)^2 = quarter m v^2. Lost fraction = (half - quarter)/half = one half.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: Rate at which a motor does work
questions.learningObjective: Compute instantaneous power from force and velocity
questions.stem: A 50 N force acts on a body moving at 4 m/s in the force direction; find power (W).
questions.explanation: Instantaneous power = F v cos theta = 50*4*1 = 200 W. When force and velocity are parallel, cos theta is 1.

questions.topic: Pressure transmission through a fluid
questions.learningObjective: Compute pressure at depth in a fluid
questions.stem: Find pressure at 10 m depth in water (density 1000 kg/m^3) above atmospheric (Pa).
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure = rho g h = 1000*9.8*10 = 98000 Pa. Atmospheric pressure is not included in gauge pressure.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: Buoyant force on a submerged object
questions.learningObjective: Compute apparent weight of submerged object
questions.stem: A 5 kg object (volume 0.002 m^3) is submerged in water; find apparent weight (N).
questions.explanation: True weight = 5*9.8 = 49 N. Buoyant force = 1000*0.002*9.8 = 19.6 N. Apparent weight = 49 - 19.6 = 29.4 N.
